name: Carver Roboweld
summary: Carver Roboweld makes welding consumables (metal-cored wires, welding rods, gouging electrodes) at a plant in Rajkot, Gujarat, and rents welding robots and regenerates forging dies through service units in Pune, Ludhiana and Hosur; all of its revenue comes from the forging industry. On a standalone basis revenue grew from ₹21.7 cr in FY24 to ₹27.0 cr in FY26, while profit more than doubled in FY26 to ₹3.5 cr as margins widened. The top ten customers gave about 81% of FY26 revenue, and operating cash flow was negative in FY26. At the upper band the post-issue P/E is about 30x standalone FY26 profit (about 20x on consolidated profit), above the 18.2x median of the listed peers named in the RHP.

fh1.finding: Standalone revenue rose from ₹21.67 cr (FY24) to ₹27.02 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 11.7%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹21.67 cr, ₹24.86 cr, ₹27.02 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.97 in FY26 (borrowings ₹15.65 cr vs net worth ₹16.13 cr).

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose 17% (₹13.39 cr to ₹15.65 cr) while total income rose 25% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹3.11 cr, ₹4.56 cr, ₹16.13 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was negative at -₹2.65 cr in FY26.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax rose 140% in FY26, from ₹1.45 cr to ₹3.48 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin rose from about 4.7% (FY24) to 5.8% (FY25) and 12.9% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 21.57% in FY26 (standalone).

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 30.1x on standalone FY26 profit (₹104.8 cr market cap vs ₹3.48 cr) vs a peer median of 18.2x (Royal Arc 18.2x, Diffusion Engineers 34.5x, Classic Electrodes 7.0x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.36x (₹104.8 cr market cap vs about ₹44.4 cr post-issue net worth) vs a peer median of about 2.25x.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: Prices of any share issues in the 12 months before the IPO were not found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold 65.77% after the issue, down from 90.07%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters was found.

is1.finding: The entire ₹28.29 cr issue is fresh; there is no offer for sale.

is2.finding: The issue is about 27% of the ₹104.8 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: No selling shareholders, because there is no offer for sale.

up1.finding: ₹11.99 cr, or 42.4% of the issue, goes to buying welding robots.

up2.finding: ₹8.60 cr, or 30.4% of the issue, goes to repaying borrowings.

up3.finding: General corporate purposes are shown at ₹7.70 cr, or 27.2% of the issue (this figure may include issue expenses).

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whose loans are being repaid beyond banks and financial institutions.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were not found in public sources.

rk1.finding: The top ten customers gave 80.78% of FY26 revenue, and all revenue comes from the forging industry.

rk2.finding: The top ten suppliers gave 92.43% of FY26 purchases and reliance on a few suppliers is called out as a risk; single-supplier shares are not published.

rk3.finding: Incorporated in August 2009, so about 17 years of operating history.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
